source.title: Sharpness & Shift-Aware Self-Supervised Learning
source.authors: Ngoc N. Tran; Song Duong; Hoang Phan; Tung Pham; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung-Nghia Le

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether batch size changes held-out performance across training epochs, using self-supervised CIFAR-10 linear evaluation rather than the original studies’ settings.
record.gate_note: Only the batch-size sweep bears on a listed version. The sharpness-aware method comparisons and augmentation-shift measurements do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship in V7. Cited prior work is not recorded as a result.
record.test_reason: Section 6.3 compares held-out classification accuracy at matched epoch checkpoints across batch sizes in a new setting: contrastive self-supervised pretraining followed by linear evaluation. This bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 6.3, rather than the paper's overall conclusion. Overall, the authors argue that sharpness-aware contrastive learning and reducing positive-pair distribution shift improve downstream classification and robustness. Their batch sweep reports generally better performance with larger batches, plateauing around 1000 epochs, and a narrowing SSA-CLR–SimCLR gap.
record.recipe_differences: Self-supervised contrastive pretraining with sharpness-aware optimization and Fourier augmentation, followed by linear evaluation; the batch-size sweep compares SSA-CLR with SimCLR rather than reproducing the claim’s original settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and epoch count; the reported gap between SSA-CLR and SimCLR narrows with more epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches generally improve FGSM robust linear-evaluation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger contrastive-pretraining batches can improve downstream adversarial robustness on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharpness-aware optimization improves downstream accuracy, and Fourier augmentation reduces the measured positive-pair distribution shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware optimization and Fourier augmentation can improve contrastive representations; these intervention results do not establish V7's sharpness–generalization-gap correlation.

record.problems: The batch-sweep values are plotted without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. Results are limited to CIFAR-10 and the tested SSL/linear-evaluation setup.
record.rows_left_out: No other listed version was tested. Table 1–5 method comparisons and the sharpness-aware accuracy ablations concern the proposed SSL method or its components, not the listed version-specific outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Language models; batches beyond an established workload-dependent threshold; controlled effects of longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Correlation of magnitude-aware sharpness with measured train–test gaps at comparable training loss, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Separate SimCLR standard-accuracy batch-size results. Section 6.3 includes SimCLR in the sweep, but R1 names only SSA-CLR. Recover the method-specific trends and matched-epoch comparisons from the figure before assigning a separate verdict.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text omits readable Figure 3 curves. Directional findings rely on the authors' explicit prose; exact values, exceptions, and uncertainty cannot be recovered. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language models, workload-dependent batch thresholds, and the cited recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with weight decay or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation measure and its correlation with train–test gaps.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 contrastive pretraining with batches 64–512, compared at matched epoch checkpoints
relationships.reason: R1 reports generally better standard accuracy with larger batches. This qualifies the penalty's applicability to contrastive learning, where batch size also changes the negative-example pool; no harmful-batch threshold is established.
relationships.display_finding: Standard accuracy generally improved with larger batches at matched checkpoints, but exact accuracies were unavailable. Batch size also changed which negative examples were available during training.
